| window | k | hold | sensitivity | FA / recording | alarms / hour | latency |

| 7 | 6 | 9 | 75.0% | 4.9% | 5.2 | 6.16 s |
| 5 | 5 | 9 | 75.0% | 2.4% | 2.6 | 5.04 s |

The operating point is a clinical trade-off, not a tuned hyperparameter. Reference burden: a retrospective ICU cohort reports a median 119 alarms/patient/day, ~5/hour (Sci Rep 2022, s41598-022-26261-4), and states that no threshold defining a 'high' alarm rate exists. The default is therefore justified as roughly doubling the existing burden, not as sitting under a published safe limit. Tuned on round-1 data — re-validate on round 2 without touching it.

## Caveats that must appear alongside any of the above

1. The +/- on the file-level accuracy is RandomForest seed variation on a handful of borderline files, NOT sampling uncertainty. Quote the Wilson or bootstrap CI instead.
2. File-level majority vote depends on clip length: re-voting the same events padded to the round-2 SOP length of 60-120 s takes pull recall to 0.000 while episode detection stays at 1.000. Report episode-level metrics.
3. No anomaly file reaches the <= 25,000 count detachment spec (KES 2025 s2.1); deepest is 27,251. Check the fixation method used for these recordings before quoting a detachment claim.
4. LOOP 5 IMU signals are synthetic. No fusion number belongs in a results table.
5. Small classes: 0: Baseline n=5, 2: Peel n=10. A perfect 5/5 on the smallest of them carries a 95% CI of about 0.57-1.00, so it is not evidence of 100% performance.
6. All 81 recordings use Sensor-* columns, which the loader trusts as physical pad order without applying PAD_ORDER, while the live serial path always applies it. Accuracy figures are unaffected (the base features are permutation-invariant) but heatmaps, peel direction and the LOOP 3 figure depend on this unverified assumption. Confirm it on the bench before publishing a propagation direction.
7. Single sensor mounting (1 session). Nothing here shows generalisation to a re-attached patch.
